questions.q: How is a KPI view built in Tableau?
options: By using only Text marks with conditional formatting
Tableau has a dedicated 'KPI' mark type separate from Shape
By connecting to a specialized KPI data source
A threshold calculation (e.g., IF SUM([Sales]) > 25000 THEN "Above Goal" ELSE "Below Goal" END) is mapped to the Shape mark, so a shape like a check or an X displays instead of a raw number
questions.explain: A KPI view is a threshold calculation assigned to the Shape property on the Marks card — Tableau's own documentation builds this exact pattern with a green check for values over goal and a red X for values under it.

questions.q: What are the three visual components of a bullet graph?
options: A pie chart layered with a scatter plot
Three separate bars of equal width with no reference elements
A single number with no visual elements at all
A bar for the actual value, a tick mark or line for the target, and shaded bands for qualitative ranges
questions.explain: A bullet graph replaces a gauge/speedometer widget with a bar (actual), a reference line (target), and reference distribution bands (qualitative ranges like poor/satisfactory/good).

questions.q: How do you swap which measure is the bar and which is the reference line in a bullet graph?
options: Delete the worksheet and rebuild it from scratch
Right-click the axis and select Swap Reference Line Fields
Change the data type of one of the measures
This cannot be changed once the bullet graph is built
questions.explain: Right-clicking the axis and choosing Swap Reference Line Fields lets you switch which measure drives the bar and which drives the reference line.

questions.q: Does Tableau have a dedicated 'Sparkline' mark type or chart option?
options: Yes — it's available only when connected to a live database
No — a sparkline is built from an ordinary line chart with headers hidden and gridlines removed, then shrunk small
No — sparklines are impossible to build in Tableau
Yes — it's a built-in option in the Show Me panel
questions.explain: Tableau has no distinct Sparkline mark type. The effect is achieved with standard formatting: hide both axis headers, remove gridlines, and shrink the worksheet so it reads as a small inline trend shape.

questions.q: In the KPI view example, what does putting Sub-Category on Rows and Region on Columns achieve, combined with the Shape-based threshold?
options: A grid where a viewer can scan every sub-category/region combination at a glance and immediately spot which ones are below goal
It hides all sub-categories that are below goal
It has no visual effect — Rows and Columns don't matter for KPI views
It automatically sorts sub-categories by total sales
questions.explain: Crossing Sub-Category and Region produces a full grid of check/X shapes, letting a viewer instantly spot every red X across the whole grid — far faster to scan than a text table of raw numbers.
